📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The conversion of the automotive industry over to electric vehicles, sold as a foregone conclusion by many car brands in the early 2020s, may have largely stalled out in America, but the picture is far different globally.
  • And the global increase came despite falling sales in China.
  • In a recent development, meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The conversion of the automotive industry over to electric vehicles, sold as a foregone conclusion by many car brands in the early 2020s, may have largely stalled out in America, but the picture is far different globally. According to data from the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, EVs now account for 31 percent of all passenger vehicle sales.

And the global increase came despite falling sales in China. The major driver of electric vehicle sales has been Europe; European EV sales have risen 37 percent year over year so far in 2026, climbing to 43 percent of the fresh vehicle sales market. CommBank data also indicated substantial growth rates in countries such as Brazil (EV sales up 164 percent, to a 13 percent market share) and India (EV sales up 76 percent, to a 9 percent market share). Even in Japan, where manufacturers have been notably EV-reticent, sales jumped 80 percent year-over-year to 5 percent of the market.

In a recent development, meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year. According to Cox Automotive data, EV sales made up 6.4 percent of the new car market in Q3 of 2026, down from more than 10 percent in Q3 of 2025. Fuel prices have been elevated this year, but that has led Americans to gravitate toward hybrids rather than fully electric vehicles. Total electrified vehicles now account for nearly 25 percent of the American market.

According to recent reports, much of the decline has been a direct result of Trump administration policies. Last year, the U.S. eliminated a $7500 federal tax credit for electric cars, which—due to a commercial vehicle loophole—made them especially cheap for buyers to lease; the 10 percent share of sales in Q3 2025 came from a glut of sales as buyers rushed to take advantage of the tax credits before they expired. Congress is also considering imposing an annual federal tax on electric cars.

Industry observers note that the Trump administration has also effectively eliminated enforcement of America’s CAFE standards, which would have effectively forced manufacturers to sell EVs to avoid hefty fines. American laws and tariffs also effectively prohibit importing affordable Chinese-made EVs, which have been a major reason behind the sales increase in Europe.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Recent findings suggest that pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

According to recent reports, interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

According to recent reports, if you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected.
  • In a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," said study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected. Researchers at The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) have now uncovered a surprising pattern: Certain regions of the heart appear to be hotspots for aging-related inflammation, offering new clues about how the heart changes over time.

In a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root. These areas contain immune cells and connective tissue cells whose interactions change with age, potentially affecting the surrounding heart muscle. The findings provide a newly introduced picture of cardiac aging and could guide future efforts to understand cardiovascular disease.

Recent findings suggest that "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," said study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX. "We really have to think of aging as something that is not linear, because just like we know that people don't age at the same rate, what we know now is that organs and tissues don't age at the same rate either, even within one individual.".

It has been revealed that much of the previous research on heart aging has centered on cardiac muscle, particularly the left ventricle. This chamber performs the essential task of pumping blood into the aorta and throughout the body. By studying the heart as a whole, rather than concentrating primarily on its muscle, the JAX team uncovered important changes in other tissues and the ways their cells interact.

According to recent reports, "The valves and the major blood vessels are parts often thought of as plumbing rather than the main engine, but this is a very complicated little machine," Rosenthal noted. "It turns out they're home to many of the cells we're interested in, and that's where some of the most important aging-related signals were concentrated.".

Mapping Hidden Hotspots of Heart Aging.

In a recent development, growing older is the single greatest risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet many of the cellular processes responsible for the heart's decline remain poorly understood. One challenge is that mammalian heart muscle cells have very little ability to regenerate or replace themselves. To investigate what happens as the heart ages, Rosenthal and her colleagues used advanced techniques that allowed them to study thousands of individual cells from young and old mice while also identifying their locations within the heart.

It has been revealed that scientists already know that aging is accompanied by a persistent, low level of inflammation throughout the body. Earlier studies have found similar changes in the heart, including an increase in immune cells that regulate inflammatory activity (macrophages) and cells that produce and maintain connective tissue and contribute to scar formation (fibroblasts).

According to recent reports, the new analysis showed that aging macrophages became more active in genes involved in inflammation and changes to tissue structure. Fibroblasts, meanwhile, increasingly displayed molecular characteristics associated with fibrosis (or scarring). Crucially, the researchers went beyond identifying which genes were active. They also mapped the locations of these cells, making it possible to see how different regions of the heart change as they grow older.

This approach revealed that inflammation and fibrosis (or scarring) were not distributed uniformly. Instead, the strongest signals appeared around the heart valves and aortic root. The researchers believe these regions may act as important centers of cardiac aging, where changes in supporting cells could influence the health of nearby heart muscle.

According to recent reports, "To keep muscle cells happy, the other cells in the heart have to continue supporting them throughout life," Rosenthal mentioned. "What this study does, for the first time, is provide a comprehensive picture of how those support cells, particularly fibroblasts and macrophages, change with age and contribute to what we call inflammaging.".

Surprising Signs of Aging in Young Hearts.

In a recent development, another unexpected discovery challenged assumptions about how scientists identify aging cells. The team examined molecular markers frequently associated with cellular senescence, a state in which cells permanently lose the ability to divide, often because of aging or stress. As senescent cells accumulate, they can contribute to ongoing inflammation, tissue damage, and diseases associated with older age.

Recent findings suggest that surprisingly, some of these supposedly age-related markers were already present in young mouse hearts. Their presence suggests that the markers alone cannot reliably establish whether a cell has entered senescence, and that their meaning may depend on where they appear and the condition of the surrounding tissue.

"What surprised us was that some of these markers that have been associated with aging were already present in young hearts. They weren't where anyone expected to find them, and that forced us to rethink what those markers are telling us," Rosenthal said. "That turns the usual interpretation of cardiac aging on its ear because these markers alone don't mean a cell is senescent. There's nothing senescent about a six-month-old mouse heart.".

According to recent reports, the researchers also identified genes that became more active with age and were especially prominent in the same regions. Among them were Ccl8, which helps transmit inflammatory signals, and Cdkn1a (also known as p21), a gene widely used as an indicator of cellular senescence. Their locations provided further evidence that the valves and aortic root may be particularly important areas for understanding how the heart ages.

It has been revealed that "We're not talking about single genes. We're talking about an entire conversation between immune cells and fibroblasts. As the heart ages, the way those cells communicate changes, and that shift appears to be linked to the inflammation and tissue remodeling we see in older hearts," Rosenthal said.

Male and Female Hearts Show Different Aging Patterns.

The study uncovered another important distinction: Aging did not produce exactly the same molecular changes in male and female mouse hearts.

Recent findings suggest that in males, aging fibroblasts showed stronger connections to biological processes associated with fibrosis. In females, the corresponding changes were more closely related to pathways involved in heart development and protein production.

Industry observers note that rosenthal noted that these differences may offer clues about cardiovascular aging in humans. Heart disease tends to become more common in women after menopause, while its development in men generally follows a more gradual pattern. The distinct cellular changes observed in male and female mice could help researchers investigate the biological processes behind these differences.

However, the results describe differences in molecular activity, not demonstrated differences in heart function or disease risk. Further research will be needed to determine how these patterns influence cardiovascular health.

Recent findings suggest that to explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the team compared the mouse results with previously published data from human hearts. Several molecular processes associated with aging, including pathways involved in responding to cellular stress, appeared in both species. This overlap suggests that at least some of the biological changes identified in mice may also be relevant to human heart aging.

"Our findings change the focus from aging across the entire heart to specific anatomical hotspots, helping us better understand how inflammation and fibrosis are connected and which regions of the heart are involved in the aging process," said study author Amalia Sintou, a postdoctoral associate at JAX.

Could These Discoveries Help Protect Aging Hearts?

Although the research does not yet identify a newly introduced treatment, it offers scientists a more detailed understanding of where aging-related changes occur and which cells are involved. By revealing these cellular patterns, the findings could help guide future studies aimed at reducing cardiovascular decline, maintaining healthy heart function, and improving health later in life.

According to recent reports, rosenthal's team is now examining whether exercise, diet, and disease alter the interactions between immune cells and connective tissue cells. The researchers hope to distinguish the normal effects of aging from changes that may leave the heart increasingly vulnerable to cardiovascular problems.

The experimental design also helped the team isolate aging itself as a contributing factor. Because the mice lived under the same conditions and received the same diet, the researchers could investigate age-related changes without the additional variation introduced by different environments or eating habits.

It has been revealed that "Valve replacement is common in older adults, and one of the massive questions is how much of the underlying damage is driven by aging itself," said study author Aleksandra Aljakna Khan, a postdoctoral associate at JAX. "Because all of the mice in our study lived in the same environment and ate the same diet, we were able to isolate the effects of aging and show that aging alone can initiate some of these changes in the valves and aorta.".

Sources indicate that together, the findings suggest that understanding heart aging requires looking beyond the muscle responsible for pumping blood. The valves, major blood vessels, and supporting cells may play a much larger role than previously recognized. Learning how these structures change and communicate over time could eventually help scientists identify ways to preserve cardiovascular health as people age.

Research Funding and Study Authors.

The research received funding from the NIH Common Fund through The Jackson Laboratory Senescence Tissue Mapping Center (JAX-Sen TMC U54 AG079753). Additional support came from JAX's National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center (P30 CA034196).

Recent findings suggest that additional authors from The Jackson Laboratory included Yue Zhao, Antonios Somarakis, Harshpreet Chandok, Juliana Alcoforado Diniz, Ramalakshmi Ramasamy, Gretchen T. Clark, Brian S. White, Paul Robson, Ron Korstanje, and J. Matthew Mahoney. Leon Frommer and Sikander Hayat of RWTH Aachen University also contributed to the study.

Materials provided by Jackson Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that automakers love to lean on nostalgia.
  • Sources indicate that fullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States.
  • It has been revealed that now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that automakers love to lean on nostalgia. Whether it’s a new paint job inspired by an old race car, or reviving a classic nameplate for a new model, utilizing a rich history can be an easy way to grab customers’ attention. But what if a company leaned on the heritage of other automakers? That’s where FullGood Motor, a Chinese company that builds modern plug-in hybrids inspired by classic cars, steps in, and FullGood now wants to break into the U.S. market.

Sources indicate that fullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States. The tech giant was formed back in 1995 as a motorcycle business called Loose Motor, and didn’t get into the automobile business until 2009. In fact, the pivot to cars was initially based out of a factory in California, before the company moved its operations to Beijing, China, in 2018, adopting the FullGood name in 2022.

See all results for used cars for sale near 51503.

It has been revealed that now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States. The company notes business is strong in China, where its factory has a 100,000-unit-per-year capacity, hence the desire to expand. We spoke with the company’s vice president, Erelly Cai, at the LA auto show to understand a bit more about the brand’s desire to come to the U.S. and the potential hurdles it might face.

The firm knows it can’t enter the U.S. market alone, especially in an era where regulations make it nigh on impossible for Chinese automakers to import their vehicles. FullGood acknowledges this challenge and is in Los Angeles seeking to talk with investors and potential American manufacturing and distribution partners.

The proposal is to export vehicles from China in component form, and then complete final assembly in the U.S. The vehicles would then be sold and registered under its American partners’ brand. It also wants to develop more vehicles directly inspired by midcentury American design.

FullGood brought one of its cars to the show, a seven-seat van named the Summer that is undoubtedly inspired by the Volkswagen Type 2, better known as the Microbus. Like all of its models, the Summer uses a plug-in hybrid powertrain. The Summer pairs a turbocharged 1.5-liter engine with electric motors from Wuling, a large and well-established Chinese automaker, and a 28-kWh battery from CATL. The front-wheel-drive powertrain produces a combined 325 hp, with electric-only driving range listed at 93 miles and total range at 497 miles. The Summer costs the equivalent of $49,000 at current exchange rates.

See all results for used cars for sale near 51503.

Recent findings suggest that cai remarked that the firm would likely use the same powertrain if it manages to introduce its vehicles to the U.S. market, with the bigger obstacle being the car’s software. The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Connected Vehicle Rule bans foreign-made cars that feature certain connected software and hardware from China and Russia. Some companies that import from China, such as Volvo, have been granted an exemption, while others, like Polestar, have been banned from the U.S.

Sources indicate that fullGood hopes the LA show can help it find a partner, so “maybe we can solve the problem together,” Cai said. The idea would be to replace the software with a new setup for the U.S. market, while keeping things like the chassis, powertrain, and interior trimmings unchanged. Along with the Summer, FullGood’s current planned lineup includes the Dolphin, which looks like a C1 Corvette; the Rocket, which emulates the 1959 Cadillac Eldorado; and the HotRod, which looks like a Ford Model A.

If FullGood manages to find a partner and bring their cars to the United States, it imagines capturing a market of buyers who are nostalgic for vehicles from their past. “They have their childhood memories,” Cai said, with FullGood’s vehicles helping to “bring those memories back.” While FullGood is still a long way from getting its cars to our shores, they certainly provide a different attitude than the current crop of vehicles sold in the U.S., with their cheery, whimsical designs, and while the barrier to getting here is high, we’re curious to see where FullGood’s Los Angeles appearance takes the oddball tech giant.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

Sources indicate that according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Recent findings suggest that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

It has been revealed that zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Recent findings suggest that respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Industry observers note that zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

Breaking: This 500 kWh energy storage system runs on retired EV batteries

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road.
  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s new Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment claims its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

“We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” noted Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Moment Energy indicates Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

According to recent reports, that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders.
  • The findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins.
  • Industry observers note that mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.

The findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.

Industry observers note that mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.

Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms.

The discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.

Worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling notable features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.

Sources indicate that to investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.

The researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.

"We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," claims Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12.".

Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?

To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.

These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.

In a recent development, although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.

In a recent development, the discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.

Recent findings suggest that "Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide fresh insights into human diseases," states Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term.".

The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is A Two-Seat Track-Ready EV

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending substantial money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge.
  • Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID.
  • Sources indicate that that remarked, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending substantial money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge. The latest showpiece is the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, a one-off electric hatchback built for the track that sheds a set of doors and borrows the electric motor from its bigger brothers.

Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID. Polo GTI and the upcoming ID.3 GTI, and its purpose is to show what the German brand can do with its modular MEB+ platform. In fact, Volkswagen is calling itself the “master of modular platforms,” proudly saying that the same architecture that underpins the bog-standard ID. Polo is capable of impressive extremes, from the ultra-efficient Mission Efficiency to the performance-oriented GTI Clubsport EV.

Sources indicate that that remarked, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy. Engineers had to take an APP550 electric motor, which was originally designed for rear-wheel-drive models like the ID.7 and ID. Tiguan, and adapt it for the ID. Polo chassis, which is front-wheel-drive.

Sources indicate that to fit the larger drive unit in the small hatchback, the whole front section of the car had to be modified, which meant designing and building an entirely fresh subframe. The longitudinal chassis members, stabilizer bar, several mounting points, and various chassis components also had to be redesigned to make the taller APP550 drive unit fit under the hood.

It has been revealed that what’s more, the high-voltage charger, air conditioning compressor, thermal management module, and the water pump had to be relocated. Designers and engineers worked together to develop special holders, adapters, and mounting concepts to make it all work.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept’s powertrain makes 362 horsepower and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton-meters) of torque, making it the most powerful electric Polo ever made. Compared to the road-going ID. Polo GTI, it makes 139 more horsepower and 192 more pound-feet of torque.

Yet, the car is still front-wheel drive. And if you’ve driven a relatively torquey EV with FWD, you know that transferring everything that an electric drive unit can give to the front wheels can prove difficult. But Volkswagen has that covered with an electronic front differential lock that uses a multiplate clutch. With it, the car can transfer power to both wheels if one of them starts to lose traction.

According to recent reports, all of that power and torque give the electric track car a zero-to-62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) sprint time of 4.7 seconds and a 149 miles pr hour (240 kilometers per hour) top speed. To enable this level of performance, the 52-kilowatt-hour battery, which is the same as in the production ID. Polo GTI, was tweaked to allow for a higher power output of up to 290 kW, as well as longer discharge periods at high outputs.

Hooked to a DC fast charger, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can take up to 105 kW, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI, which can go from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.

The extra power and torque go hand in hand with plenty of changes to the body and underneath it. The one-off EV is 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) wider than the production model and sits 30 mm (1.1 in) lower than the standard ID. Polo. The same adaptive suspension as the production vehicle is used, but its setup is adjusted for track use.

The electric Clubsport Concept has just two doors instead of the regular ID. Polo’s four, and features a pretty aggressive body kit with wide wheel arches, functional air ducts, and a huge rear wing. GTI badges and red accents are everywhere, including in the interior, where the central touchscreen no longer acts as the infotainment center. In fact, the concept doesn’t have an infotainment system, as the central screen handles driving settings exclusively.

Bright red five-point harnesses protect the driver and front passenger sitting in Recaro racing bucket seats, while a red rollover bar has replaced the rear seats and cargo area.

Industry observers note that the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is not yet intended for production, but the German automaker hasn’t ruled out the option entirely, saying that it has always associated the development of concept vehicles “with the theoretical option of turning a one-off into a latest production derivative.”.

The track-focused EV will make its first live appearance at the Essen Motor Show in Germany, which runs from November 27 through December 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re in downtown Los Angeles now through November 29 and want to get an up-close-and-personal look at some cool cars, head over to the convention center to see what’s poppin’ at the annual auto show. However, if you don’t have time to make the trip—or you’re nowhere near L.A.—and want to see the best cars that this year’s event had to offer, we've got you covered. While the 2026 L.A. auto show was short on major debuts or futuristic concepts, it hosted several headline-catching cars as well as multiple highly anticipated new models.

It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away. While we’re highly skeptical that Tesla will ever publicly sell the thruster-equipped version that flew through the air and did a barrel roll, it’s more likely that a similar-looking, street-legal version will eventually reach production. Haters gonna hate, but the Roadster looks pretty damn cool, like Lamborghini designer Fabrizio Giugiaro was hired to style his version of the Lotus Esprit S1 that James Bond drove in The Spy Who Loved Me. Consider us shaken, not stirred.

According to recent reports, being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins. Like meeting the actor who famously played Hannibal Lecter, meeting one of the most iconic supercars ever made is unnerving. Now, you may have noticed that this example isn’t exactly all original; instead, it has been modified by Phiaro Inc., and it features a custom widebody kit as well as a chameleon-like paint job. The best part? Its modifications are completely reversible. Let’s just say it drew a crowd.

In a recent development, genesis is going after the throats of luxury stalwarts like BMW, Mercedes-Benz and—dare we say—Bentley with the latest GV90. The one you see here is the top-of-the-line Neolun model, and its most distinctive feature is these gigantic coach doors. Inside are four VIP-grade seats that treat passengers to an opulent cabin awash in rich materials and front seats that swivel 180 degrees to create a mobile lounge (this configuration is only accessible when the 657-hp EV is parked). The GV90 Neolun also has a veneer wood floor and 24-inch wheels that remind us of the iconic monoblock wheels made famous by Mercedes-AMG and Brabus. Few SUVs turn our heads, but Genesis appears to have another game-changer on its metaphorical hands.

Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept.

It has been revealed that we spotted this beautiful wagon-like Toyota Crown Signia from across the convention center’s south hall. Among a sea of generic crossovers, this low-slung longroof is an ode to an age when most Americans didn’t lust after the elevated seating position of a semi-truck. Of course, if you haven’t noticed, this isn’t exactly a production-spec Crown Signia. If you read our recent SEMA coverage, you may recognize it as the GT-S concept. Along with being lowered by five inches and wearing flared fenders that resemble the Mustang GTD, it has custom one-off coil-over dampers, 21-inch HRE wheels, and brakes from a Lexus RX500h F Sport. To all that, we say, “Hell yeah, brother!”.

Recent findings suggest that let’s take a break from the world of flying cars, Bugattis, and fanciful electric SUVs to enjoy something that most people can afford: the upcoming eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra. If its disorienting front lighting, heavily creased bodywork, and broad haunches intimidate you, we’re sure there’s a safer-looking alternative in Toyota’s showroom. But whatever you may think about the new Elantra’s styling, it definitely attracts attention. And Hyundai is hoping it’ll do just that to new customers who are looking to join the brand’s family tree. The nonhybrid version seen here draws power from a humble 147-hp four-cylinder engine, but the lineup will add a more powerful hybrid model sometime next year. While pricing is still TBD, we expect that it’ll cost around $25,000 to own the most interesting car in your cul-de-sac.

Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition.

Sources indicate that if you’ve ever watched an episode of Overhaulin’, a TV show that lasted for 10 seasons on TLC, then you’ve heard of custom car designer Chip Foose. Now, he has teamed up with Fox Factory Vehicles to create this even more muscular version of the latest Ram 1500 Rumble Bee street truck. Along with unique wheels and body graphics, the interior has been restyled with diamond-stitched seats and Foose branding. The truck itself has a lowered ride height with an aftermarket coil-over suspension, and its supercharged V-8 is available with either 705 or 1000 horsepower. That’s a lot of horsies, and they’ll cost customers a lot of cash, with the Rumble Bee Foose Edition starting at $154,990.

It has been revealed that this was one of the few concept cars at the show, but the Acura Nexera was first revealed back in August during Monterey Car Week. Still, the futuristic concept is really cool to see in person, especially with its dramatic glass canopy. Plus, how many times have you seen an Acura with butterfly doors? While the Nexera doesn’t preview an upcoming production model, it does provide a glimpse of Acura’s next-generation design language. Will the fresh 2028 RDX feature an active rear spoiler, carbon-fiber accents, and lighting that glows through the bodywork? Probably not. However, we can expect to see some of the Nexera concept’s interesting styling influence the brand’s next-gen compact SUV.

Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition.

Industry observers note that if you’re old enough to remember Acura’s legendary DC2 Integra Type R, you’ll definitely appreciate this newly introduced Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Not only does its Blazing Phoenix Yellow call more attention to itself than Big Bird starring in an old-timey picture show, but it also honors the OG Type R, which also wore a shade of Phoenix Yellow. The modern-day throwback sport compact packs the same 320-hp turbo four and six-speed manual as other models, but this one alone has copper-colored wheels and a titanium shift knob from the Honda Civic Type R. To get one in your driveway, you’ll need to be lucky enough to score one of the 700 limited copies for the U.S. market, but the asking price is a reasonable $58,995.

According to recent reports, have you been waiting for Dodge to stuff a Hemi V-8 in the latest Charger? Well, you’re going to have to keep waiting for a while. However, if you’ve been hoping that the Brotherhood of Muscle will make a gas-powered Charger that’s set up for quick lap times, the new Super Bee variant should help you scratch that itch. Along with exclusive aero bits, stronger brakes, and wider summer tires, this track-focused Charger features an enhanced high-output Hurricane twin-turbo 3.0-liter straight-six, which is good for 600 horsepower (50 more than normal). The reimagined “Super Bee” logo on the rear quarter panel is one way to separate it from its siblings, but it also has an entirely different front clip that features new headlights and more open space to inhale engine-cooling air. If you’re wondering how much it costs, so are we, so stay tuned.

Recent findings suggest that like many of you, this was our first time seeing the latest Chevy Silverado 1500’s new off-road-focused ZR2 variant. It’s a big truck, so big that we initially thought it was the HD version. Among the many changes to the newest generation of Chevy’s bestselling full-size pickup truck are all-new small-block V-8s. The ZR2 seen here is powered by a 481-hp 6.6-liter that helps churn massive all-terrain tires, which now stand 35 inches tall for the first time on a half-ton Silverado. The Ford F-150 Raptor-rivaling ZR2’s other party tricks include trick Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers. Inside, it includes GM’s first use of forged carbon fiber (neat!). If you want the most badass version, you’ll want to opt for the Bison Edition that adds beadlock-capable wheels, unique bumpers, and even more underbody armor. The cost of admission for the regular ZR2 is just under $80K, while the Bison starts even higher.

Eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive newly introduced cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage at the moment includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

  • According to recent reports, the basics are relatively straightforward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first manual C8-gen Chevrolet Corvette is running and driving only a year after Tremec unveiled its latest TR-9060 six-speed manual transaxle, and Road & Track just got a chance to take it for a spin.

Recent findings suggest that the car in question, built by Peitz Performance in Texas, is actually a race car, and it’s still in the early prototype phase. In other words, my test is not representative of what a polished and optimized road car will feel like. But it was enough to prove that the concept works.

According to recent reports, the basics are relatively straightforward. Tremec engineered this new six-speed transaxle to fit lots of different cars, from the C8 Corvette to McLarens and more. It’s for the aftermarket to play around with, as Chevy has made it clear the C8 won’t be getting a manual from the factory. Alex Peitz, the owner of Peitz Performance, had an existing relationship with Tremec, which is how he managed to get his hands on one of these transaxles before regular production of them begins. (Tremec claims it’s targeting July 2027 for initial sales to distributors.).

Already neck-deep in C8 builds, Peitz used his experience and—most importantly—3-D scans of the car. This head start helped him map out how he’d install the transmission, shift cables, clutch, and shifter before he even had the parts in hand. A heavily modified Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing clutch pedal is squeezed into the pedal box. There was some fear that the new gearbox would interfere with the exhaust system, but that ended up not being an issue once it was installed. Of all the problems to solve, though, making the C8’s complicated and advanced electrical architecture talk nicely with the manual was the toughest challenge. It’s one Peitz admits he is still sorting out.

On top of being version one of the manual C8 Corvette, Peitz’s car is a fully caged and built race car, with all the temperamental nature common to the breed. Unfortunately, when I arrived to drive it, the power steering and ABS had recently left the chat. With massive slicks mounted both front and rear, that made steering the car one hell of an arm workout. On top of that, the fixed bucket seat was, well, fixed. Peitz has longer legs than I do, and I was only just barely able to get the extremely heavy race clutch to the floor with the toe of my shoe extended as far as I could.

The good news is that the transmission itself seems to work without issue. Driving the C8, I felt instantly familiar with where each gear should be. There was no vagueness or sloppiness to be found. That mentioned, what was missing was the affirmative thud I was expecting as each gear was fully selected. The weight of the throw action was oddly light for such a powerful and torquey car, although not offensively so. But these are preferences that should hopefully be tweaked later as the aftermarket fine-tunes the action of the gearchanges with bushings and shifter design.

One thing every manualized C8 is set to struggle with is shifter placement. The car’s center console was never designed with a manual transmission in mind. It is too tall, and that presents a problem for ergonomics, as the new shifter sits inherently higher than where you expect to find it. Depending on an individual driver’s height or arm length, it may work fine, but my arm felt far too high in the air as I grabbed each gear. A shorter shifter might help, but only by making the problem less noticeable as opposed to fixing it entirely.

Rev matching was remarkably easy, although the pedal placement meant I wasn’t able to heel-and-toe. Auto rev matching will be possible, Peitz claims, and while the demonstrator doesn’t have it now, it will be an option for those who want to convert their cars in the future. And this early pedal arrangement will surely evolve as Peitz and other shops work up more polished solutions.

According to recent reports, one of the promising aspects that should not change is the gearing. I tested the car at Michigan’s newest racetrack, Motorsports Gateway, and found myself constantly shifting thanks to the relative shortness of the ratios. This is definitely a good thing; you choose a manual for the pleasure of changing gears. Porsche 718 owners know the curse of especially long gears well—if you can go over 80 mph in second gear, you end up rarely actually needing to shift on a twisting road. That won’t be the case for a C8 with the Tremec, because like with the eight-speed Tremec dual-clutch in the factory C8, you are going to stay busy stirring the pot.

Industry observers note that beyond that, at this stage, I can’t say too much about how a roadgoing C8 manual will be, but Peitz gets credit for doing the hard yards of proving it is indeed possible to get three pedals into the mid-engined Corvette. Tremec states it prepares on installing its transmission in a test car of its own next year, and that will be a bone-stock production C8. We’ll be champing at the bit to get behind the wheel of that one when it ultimately happens. But Peitz Performance deserves the credit for getting here first. The manual Corvette is back!

Industry observers note that on the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two fresh main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

BYD is preparing to launch a newly introduced flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the new flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A new creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo remarked after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

The new flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously mentioned the tech giant expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview demonstrates a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

In a recent development, the concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD said earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

According to recent reports, BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo stated to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

Latest Update: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • Recent findings suggest that quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

Recent findings suggest that quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A Newly introduced Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

The breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

Quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can quickly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

According to recent reports, rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the new approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify notable interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

Industry observers note that "From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

To evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

In a recent development, after this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, showed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

Sources indicate that the next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

In a recent development, "This is particularly important because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

It has been revealed that "After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," notes Peter Zoller.

This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how promptly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

In a recent development, the findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

It has been revealed that bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

The 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a company that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

Getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

All in all, it looks really badass and indicates that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • First up, there’s the design—inside and out.
  • Honda describes the new look as its “Grand-Journey” concept, which emphasizes clean body surfaces to deliver a modern look that hints at a sporty character and pushes owners to embark on a long, delightful drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that before we dive in here: don’t get too attached to the latest Honda Avancier you see here, because it ain’t coming to American Honda dealerships. John Cena will not be touting its delights during NFL games. But this three-row crossover is still very much worth discussing here at United States-based Road & Track, because much of what you see here will be finding its way to sedans and SUVs that are, in fact, inbound for the good ol’ U.S. of A.

First up, there’s the design—inside and out. The exterior utilizes Honda’s latest design philosophy, seen previously on a pair of sedan and SUV concepts but rendered here in a much more, shall we say, friendly form. Like many a modern machine, it moves the headlights lower on the front fascia and separates them from LED accent eyebrows above, and adds a strong grille dotted with trapezoidal shapes that boasts the latest version of the “H” front and center. The side and rear views have a hint of Range Rover to them, as well as a surprisingly racy fastback angle to the D-pillar and a spoiler that conceals the rear wiper. Recessed door handles, presumably, aim to reduce drag and boost mileage.

Honda describes the new look as its “Grand-Journey” concept, which emphasizes clean body surfaces to deliver a modern look that hints at a sporty character and pushes owners to embark on a long, delightful drive. I don’t know if I’d go quite that far, but the Avancier certainly looks a good bit fancier than the likes of the Pilot or CR-V found in dealerships today.

According to recent reports, the “Grand-Journey” language also extends to the interior of the SUV. The cockpit is clean and elegant, especially in the mint-Oreo tones seen here. In order to free up space, Honda changed the gear shift of past models to a column shifter, and moved as many functions as possible to the central display, creating what the press release describes as “a simple instrument panel free of switches and buttons.” (That said, look close, and you can make out at least what appear to be a couple rockers and tactile switches on the steering wheel, so thank heaven for small favors.).

Perhaps more excitingly, the Avancier marks the first production use of the new, admittely-not-that-interestingly-named “Honda Hybrid” powertrain system. The setup places an even greater emphasis on the electric part of the gas-electric team-up, with the internal-combustion side working directly to move the car during fast cruising but the motor propelling the vehicle the vast majority of the time. Actually, make that motors, plural: this crossover becomes the first in the line to use the tech giant’s “DualPower eAWD,” which has separate electric motors for each axle to deliver improved control during both acceleration and turning. It also gains the S+ Shift function inaugurated on the Prelude, which adds some faux gearing fun to the mix.

And the Avancier’s bones are also built fresh, as this crossover marks the inaugural use of Honda’s newest platform, meant to boost stability and driving fun. This new midsize platform, Honda indicates, can work for C- and D-segment vehicles in both sedan and SUV body styles—which, roughly, translates to the Civic, Accord, CR-V, Pilot, and Passport. The platform is designed to deliver an ergonomic, comfortable driving position, while also improving tire contact for a smoother and more dialed-in ride.

According to recent reports, so while we may never see the Avancier on our streets (unless some odd soul wants to import one come 2051), the bits and pieces that make it up are sure to be found in the next generations of some of our favorite mainstream cars. And with the all-new Honda CR-V set to debut next year and already being teased, we shouldn’t have to wait long.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla officially launched in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

Sources indicate that the launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.

According to recent reports, musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”.

JAJAJAJ QUE ES ESTO, Milei lo llamó de sorpresa a Elon Musk para que diga algo sobre el local de Tesla inaugurado y es lo mas INCÓMODO que vas a ver en tu vida, se quería ir a la mierda y COLGÓ, durísimo, ni Elon Musk lo soporta al gordo pelotudo pic.twitter.com/CrJkv4iu1x.

In a recent development, then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he remarked. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil manufacturer YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”.

And that was it. The feed cut before he even said goodbye.

Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”.

The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.

According to recent reports, tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:.

Tesla adds about $600 in reservation, destination, and documentation fees on top of that, and first deliveries aren’t expected until March or April 2027. There are no dealers. Sales happen online, with showroom space at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls in Buenos Aires.

Argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which debuted in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.

What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating "I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means" in his interview with CNBC.

Especially surprising after he declared, "I’m not just MAGA; I’m 'Dark MAGA,'" after spending half a billion dollars to support MAGA candidates, and after promoting the MAGA political agenda (which he has, in part, personally implemented through the DOGE).

At this point, I expect him to reappear in the guise of a Democrat and write a big, fat, one-billion-dollar check to a Democratic super PAC for the 2028 election cycle.

I am sure Musk has a lot on his mind right now, but selling Tesla vehicles clearly isn’t one of them, because he couldn’t come up with anything to say about it.

Industry observers note that launching a new market has one job: get people excited to buy the cars. Musk had a sitting president cheering for him on stage, a room full of fans, and every camera in Buenos Aires pointed at him. He couldn’t come up with a single reason to buy a Model Y.

This isn’t stage fright. Musk has been telling investors for two years that Tesla’s future is robotaxis and Optimus robots, not selling cars. Meanwhile, Tesla’s deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025, its second annual decline in a row. The guy who is behind the brand doesn’t care about selling these cars anymore, and this clip shows it better than anything I’ve seen.

The Red Bull Formula 1 team has a brutal reputation for chewing up promising new drivers, but Kiwi driver Liam Lawson has kept his focus after being demoted from being Max Verstappen’s teammate back to the junior Visa Cash App Racing Bulls (VCARB) team in 2025. Lawson had an excellent year with the Racing Bulls so far, including a top-10 finish and a respectable stand-in back at Red Bull over the summer filling in for an injured Isack Hadjar.

Industry observers note that despite his performance, he was unsure of his seat for 2027 until just a few days ago, when VCARB confirmed Lawson and teammate Arvid Lindblad will both return for next year. Discussion of the future was still off limits for this interview, but it was a noticeably relaxed Liam Lawson who sat down with us to talk about massive trucks, sad songs, and what makes Vegas such a tough race.

Car and Driver: What is the week leading up to a race like, especially a media-heavy one like Las Vegas?

See all results for used cars for sale near 94087.

Sources indicate that liam Lawson: Vegas is a unique race in many aspects. The timings of it [Vegas is a night race]. And then this weekend for us, this year in general with these cars, there were new regulations, new power units. Every weekend has been a bit of a challenge to learn. Vegas is very cold and not high grip, it's very, very low grip. The track’s quite dirty as well. They open the street up at night and it sort of makes it quite difficult for us when we come back the next day. So the prep that goes in is a little bit more than normal. Sources indicate that I guess I hadn’t really thought of it that way, but because the setup is so different, even tracks that you’re very familiar with are going to be almost like new tracks. Like each race you’re all running for the first time with this setup.

According to recent reports, yeah, it’s very different, especially at the start of the year. I would say things are now getting a lot more consistent as we get in the groove of things. We started probably in January, a lot earlier than normal with preseason testing and trying to get a handle on these cars.

You’re known as a pretty technical guy, a pretty technical driver. What’s your relationship with your team in terms of giving them feedback on the cars or being involved in setup?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three fresh playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major revision, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of latest content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three fresh playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

Recent findings suggest that the first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Sources indicate that speaking of elemental reactions, fresh in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

It has been revealed that then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a substantial confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the newly introduced Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

Recent findings suggest that the first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a latest outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside latest stories of the Adepti.

Sources indicate that all around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the fresh Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

The Remnants Of The Electric Saab That Never Was Are Going Up For Auction
